title: Vegetarian Butternut Lasagne
subtitle: Roasted butternut squash and spinach lasagne with béchamel
excerpt: Vegetarian butternut lasagne layers roasted butternut squash, wilted spinach, and creamy béchamel between pasta sheets. The squash is sweet and substantial where meat would be; the spinach adds a slightly bitter counterpoint. A proper alternative to the meat version rather than a compromise.
sourceNotes: A vegetarian adaptation of the classic Italian lasagne al forno, using seasonal roasted butternut squash as the main filling. Butternut squash lasagne appears throughout British vegetarian cooking from the 1990s onward.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely and freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat from frozen covered at 180°C for 50 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 24 hours ahead, refrigerate, and bake from cold adding 15 minutes covered.

content.text: Vegetarian butternut lasagne uses roasted butternut squash as the central filling. Roasting concentrates the squash's sweetness and gives it a slightly caramelised edge that works against the savoury richness of the béchamel. Spinach wilted with garlic provides a second filling layer. There is no tomato sauce here; the dish is creamier and more delicate than the meat version.

items.prepNote: peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks

content.text: Roast the squash and wilt the spinach

Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C / gas mark 6). Spread {{butternut-squash}} of squash chunks in a single layer on a roasting tin. Drizzle with 2 tablespoons of olive oil and season with half the nutmeg and half the salt. Roast for 30 to 35 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender. Set aside.

Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large frying pan. Add the {{garlic}} of sliced garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Add {{spinach}} of spinach in batches and stir until wilted, about 3 minutes. Season with remaining salt and nutmeg. Squeeze out excess liquid and chop roughly. Set aside.

Reduce the oven to 190°C (fan 170°C). Melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter in a saucepan. Add {{plain-flour}} of flour and stir for 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in {{whole-milk}} of warm milk, then stir over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes until thick. Season with a pinch of salt and nutmeg.

Spread a thin layer of béchamel on the base of a large baking tin. Lay 3 to 4 sheets of {{lasagne-sheets}} in a layer. Scatter half the roasted squash, then half the spinach. Spoon a quarter of the remaining béchamel over and scatter some {{parmesan}} of Parmesan. Repeat the layers: pasta, remaining squash, remaining spinach, béchamel, Parmesan. Finish with a final layer of pasta, the remaining béchamel, and a generous layer of Parmesan.
Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for a further 20 minutes until golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.cause: The spinach was not squeezed dry before layering, releasing water during baking.
items.fix: After wilting the spinach, press it firmly in a sieve or squeeze in a tea towel to remove as much liquid as possible before chopping and layering.

items.symptom: The squash is falling apart and mushy
items.cause: The squash was cut too small or roasted too long.
items.fix: Cut in 2 cm chunks and roast until just tender and caramelised at the edges, not until collapsing. The chunks hold their shape better when layered.

content.text: Butternut squash lasagne is an autumn and winter dish. It entered British vegetarian cooking in the 1990s as squash became more widely available in supermarkets. There is no traditional Italian equivalent, as butternut squash is not a common Italian ingredient. The construction is Italian but the filling is a British vegetarian adaptation. It works well because the squash has enough substance and flavour to carry the dish without meat.
